newsitem.title: USA: House votes to end U.S. Bosnia mission in one year.
newsitem.headline: House votes to end U.S. Bosnia mission in one year.

text.p: The House of Representatives voted on Tuesday to cut off funds for U.S. military operations in Bosnia after June 30, 1998 despite strong objections of the Pentagon that a mandatory withdrawal date could put U.S. troops in jeopardy.

President Bill Clinton has told Congress that U.S. participation in the United Nations peacekeeping mission is to end by that date, but lawmakers said they wanted to force him to request an extension if he decides the troops should remain longer.
The House voted 278-148 to cut off funding for the U.S. mission next year after rejecting an alternative which would have forced a withdrawal of the troops by Dec. 31, 1997.

Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines said the administration officials will recommend the president veto the 1998 defense authorization bill if the Bosnia withdrawal amendment is included in the final version.
The Senate is expected to vote on its version of the $268.2 billion defense bill next month. It provides authorization for Pentagon programs for fiscal 1998 which starts on Oct. 1.
